China expands, diversifies space launch infrastructure
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-31
17:42:20 UTC
02:42:20 KST

A typical example is a commercial rocket carrying nine satellites that lifted off from a ship in the East China Sea near Shanghai in September this year. Although the densely populated economic hub has no traditional rocket launch site, sea-based launches are able to connect Shanghai to the country's growing space industry.
China's first sea launch took place in 2019, off the coast of Haiyang in east China's Shandong Province. The coastal city has since built a spaceport for rocket assembly, testing and launch operations. Teng Yao, chief engineer of the spaceport, said sea launches offer greater flexibility in choosing launch locations and trajectories, and allow rocket debris to fall into waters that are unpopulated.
Wenchang in south China's Hainan Province, which hosts a launch site tasked with missions of launching space station modules and lunar probes, has added facilities specifically for commercial rocket and satellite launches since 2024.
Meanwhile, the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone near the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China has developed launch pads tailored to private rocket makers.
Access to launch pads has been a challenge for China's commercial space sector. Wang Lifeng, a professor at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, cited limited launch capacity, tight schedules and long distances between launch sites and rocket assembly facilities as constraints on growth.
Large satellite networks like Qianfan (or Spacesail) and GW constellations, which each have more than 10,000 satellites, further increase the need for a steady flow of launches.
Diversified facilities not only boost launch numbers but also make launch operations more efficient.
Wenchang's commercial spacecraft launch site has put its first two pads into regular service. The second pad alone can accommodate more than 20 rocket types and can be prepared for another launch in 66 hours. The third and fourth pads in the second phase are scheduled to be operational by the end of the year. Upon full commissioning, the site is able to handle about 60 launches annually.
Haiyang offers another route to greater efficiency. Peng Haomin, co-founder of Orienspace, said the private company's facilities are clustered in Haiyang's spaceport, allowing rockets to be assembled, tested and loaded onto a launch ship within 5 km.
"This has replaced usual transportation over more than 1,000 km, drastically cutting logistics time and cost," Peng said.
Dedicated facilities can also streamline rocket operations. Meng Xiangfu, deputy chief commander of Lijian-1 rocket of commercial spaceflight company CAS Space, said that with its tailored launch pad and technical facilities at the Dongfeng commercial space innovation pilot zone, the company can complete the testing and preparation of a rocket in 10 days.
The expansion of launch infrastructure not only benefits the space industry, but also helps boost local economy through investment.
With more than 30 aerospace projects landed, Haiyang has attracted 33.5 billion yuan (around 5 billion U.S. dollars) in related investment. Wenchang's space industry park hosts over 700 companies, while Shanghai is developing a commercial spaceport-related terminal to link rocket assembly with port logistics and sea launch services.
These developments fit into a broader global trend of investing in space capabilities to support the sector's growth, as the United States aims at expanding its space transportation capabilities and Russia calls for efforts to upgrade its industrial and ground-based space infrastructure.
A 2025-2027 action plan issued by the China National Space Administration calls for coordinated development of commercial space launch sites and supports new types of commercial launch systems, including sea-based launch and recovery facilities.
At the same time, China is pressing ahead with the development of heavy-lift and reusable launch vehicles to further expand launch capacity and improve cost efficiency.
Analysts note that efficient operation of these facilities could equip China's commercial space sector with the launch capacity and operational flexibility it needs.

Protests, fueled by high cost of living, hit streets in France and Germany
Major cities in France and Germany were the scenes of protests on Saturday. Protesters in Paris, the capital, began marching from Porte de Bagnolet.

The protests were unfolding “without any notable incidents”, the ministry added at the time.
Police had made 27 arrests by 2pm local time, AFP reported.
Demonstrations were largely peaceful through the afternoon, though police fired tear gas in Lyon, France’s third-largest city, and Toulouse in the southwest, while tension also broke out at the end of the march in Marseille, Reuters reported.
Also, thousands of young Germans took to the streets nationwide in the latest protests in Europe led by youths angry at political elites they say are ignoring their concerns.
In Berlin, Frankfurt, Cologne and dozens of other cities, demonstrators turned out for the protests organized by the group "GenZ regelt!" (GenZ has got this).
They have been inspired by similar movements across Europe, including in France and Italy. Thousands of police were deployed nationwide and some shops boarded up their windows, with authorities fearful violence could break out.
There were reports of fireworks at some protests and several arrests, although the demonstrations appeared mostly peaceful by the early evening.
Demonstrators waved signs that read: "Time for resistance", and "Merz must go", in reference to conservative Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
Germany was in contact with officials in France and Italy amid fears that radicals from overseas could seek to join the German protests.
"We're taking to the streets for a life that everyone can afford," said Veronika Dinter, a spokeswoman for the "GenZ regelt!" movement.
"Hardly anyone still believes in a better future if everything just continues as it is."
The movement's complaints range from the high cost of living to poorly maintained schools, government spending cuts and, more broadly, what it sees as politicians making decisions with apparently little regard for the younger generation.
They are also unhappy with sharply increased military spending and a new voluntary service model aimed at boosting troop numbers, fearing it is a step towards bringing back conscription.
But the numbers of protesters appeared below those hoped for by organizers.

GIZA, Egypt - A minibus collided with a heavy truck on a highway west of Cairo on Oct 31, killing 10 people and injuring 24 others, Egypt’s health ministry said.

Pressure mounts on UK government to launch inquiry into Britain’s role in Gaza
Over 50,000 people in the UK have signed a petition urging the government to launch an inquiry into Britain’s role in the war in Gaza, which has been determined to be a genocide by scholars and leading rights groups.
The petition aims to garner 100,000 signatures in order to force the matter to be discussed in the House of Commons.
As of Saturday, 56,947 people have signed the petition, with many demanding a thorough investigation into Britain’s role in the war, including through sales and supply of weapons to Israel.
The petition was started by Jennifer Forbes, a former Labour parliamentary candidate for the Truro and Falmouth constituency.
Signatories of the petition have asserted that the UK has played a vital role in the genocide through providing reconnaissance aircraft and allowing the use of Royal Air Force bases.
The mounting pressure comes as dozens of MPs in recent months, including prominent members of the Labour Party, have been pushing for such an inquiry; however, the government is yet to respond.
The petition urges that the inquiry must be carried out independently of the government so that the commission of inquiry has the power to question ministers and government officials involved in the decision-making processes, particularly regarding what is believed to be British complicity in Israeli war crimes.
Those who have signed the petition have also called for clear answers on the types of weapons supplied to Israel, the reasons behind the UK’s involvement as well as disclosure of intelligence gathered during RAF sorties over Gaza amid the war.
The petition states that the investigation should also reveal details on legal advice the British government sought during its assessment of whether genocide has occurred in Gaza.
Israel’s war on Gaza, which started in October 2023, has killed over 74,000 Palestinians. The war has plunged the enclave into a deep humanitarian crisis, levelled entire neighbourhoods and displaced much of the population.
Despite an October 2025 ceasefire, Israel has continued to violate the terms of the truce and has carried out near-daily killings and demolitions.
Israel has also failed to abide by its aid obligations and has continued to restrict vital emergency aid from entering the Strip through land crossings.
Earlier this year, independent MP Jeremy Corbyn has vowed to expose Britain's complicity in Gaza and pursue accountability for Palestine after reintroducing a bill calling for an independent inquiry into the UK's role in Israel's war.
In comments made to The New Arab in June, he said his efforts were driven by a determination to avoid the delays that followed the Iraq war, when years passed before an inquiry was established and a report published detailing failures within the British government's decision-making process.

Jordan stops armed group from attempting to enter from Syria, armed forces say
Oct 31 - Jordanian border guards stopped a group of 14 armed individuals attempting to cross into the country from Syria, state news agency Petra quoted the armed forces as saying on Saturday.
They tried to infiltrate on Friday under heavy fire and direct engagement, causing numerous casualties among the group. Some fled back into Syria, the armed forces said.
The report could not be found on Petra's website later in the day. No correction had been issued by Saturday evening.
Petra did not elaborate on the identity of the 14 people.
Jordan faces persistent security challenges along its border with Syria, including drug and weapons smuggling. Networks have employed increasingly sophisticated tactics to transport narcotics across the border.
The attempted infiltration came after Jordan launched airstrikes on southern Syria on Monday, saying it targeted hideouts of militant groups it linked to a deadly attack on a church in Jordan earlier this month. It said more than 20 Islamic State militants were killed in the strikes.
Nine people were killed and at least 34 wounded when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud, in Jordan's southern Karak governorate, on October 23.
King Abdullah ordered an "iron fisted" response by security forces to the highly unusual attack on Jordan's Christian minority, which he and other top officials blamed on "extremist terrorists".
Islamic State, which was defeated by a US-led coalition, has been trying to make a comeback in neighboring Iraq and Syria, where it once controlled large areas.
Jordan, a US partner in the fight against Islamist militant groups, is regarded as a relatively stable state in the Middle East. Its security services have foiled plots by Islamist militants in the past, including suspected Islamic State supporters.
Jordan's strikes on southern Syria created tensions between Amman and Damascus, with Syria condemning them as a violation of its sovereignty and saying they had killed seven civilians, including three children and a woman. Jordan's foreign minister expressed regret over civilian casualties and reaffirmed Amman's respect for Syria's sovereignty.
The two countries agreed to establish a joint security committee to investigate the strikes and their aftermath and strengthen intelligence sharing and coordination on the ground.
BORDER SECURITY COOPERATION
Relations between Jordan and Syria had improved following the ousting of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad in December 2024. They stepped up cooperation on border security, trade and efforts to combat drug trafficking and militant groups.
The recent airstrikes, however, have tested that rapprochement, although both sides have sought to ease strains through renewed security coordination.
"There is a lot of cooperation with Iraq, Jordan and Lebanon in order to guarantee the security and stability of the borders. Our region is facing lots of challenges, however, with cooperation we can overcome the challenges," Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said at the Manama Dialogue conference in Bahrain on Saturday. Araghchi: Iran has no plans for talks with US until its conditions are met
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-31
17:27:29 UTC
02:27:29 KST

Araghchi: Iran has no plans for talks with US until its conditions are met
TEHRAN — Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said Iran has no plans to hold talks with the United States under the current circumstances, stressing that Tehran will consider direct or indirect negotiations only after Washington accepts its conditions.
In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi discussed the latest diplomatic efforts, a message conveyed by US Vice President JD Vance, proposals put forward by regional mediators, Iran’s conditions regarding the Strait of Hormuz, and the country's military preparedness amid the possibility of renewed confrontation.
He said the message sent by Vance had been carefully reviewed and discussed at high-level meetings in Iran. Araghchi described the initiative to open a channel for dialogue as a positive development, but warned that Washington would be making another mistake if it sought to exploit the initiative to create divisions within Iran.
“The American side’s attempt to open the door to dialogue and broader understanding is a positive step,” he said, adding that if the purpose was to sow discord, it would amount to another mistake by the United States.
Araghchi rejected speculation about an imminent meeting between Iranian and American officials, saying no such meeting was currently planned and that media reports on the matter did not reflect Tehran’s position.
“We see no need to meet with the Americans at present,” he said, emphasizing that Iran’s conditions were clear and that regional mediators were continuing their consultations on the basis of those conditions.
He added that Iran would decide whether any future negotiations should be held directly or indirectly only after the United States agreed to its demands.
Mediators continue diplomatic consultations
Araghchi said regional mediators were continuing their efforts to facilitate an understanding between Tehran and Washington. He noted that Qatar and Pakistan remained involved in the consultations and that an Iranian official had traveled to Qatar to pursue discussions.
“My aide is currently in Qatar to continue consultations,” he said.
The foreign minister also referred to proposals submitted by mediators concerning Iran’s nuclear program, saying Tehran was examining them as part of the second phase of the diplomatic process.
Addressing Iran’s relations with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Araghchi said a considerable distance remained before cooperation with the agency could return to normal.
He stressed that Iran remains a party to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) and is committed to fulfilling its obligations under the treaty. Iran’s position on its nuclear commitments, he indicated, should be considered separately from the current difficulties surrounding cooperation with the IAEA.
Iran sets conditions for reopening Strait of Hormuz
Araghchi also outlined Iran’s proposal concerning the Strait of Hormuz, explaining that discussions with Qatari mediators had led to a significant reduction in the proposed implementation period.
He said the Qatari side had initially suggested a five-day period for implementing the proposal, but subsequent consultations had reduced the timeframe to two days.
The Iranian proposal includes several conditions, among them the lifting of sanctions imposed following the Islamabad memorandum, a reduction in the US military presence in the region, the restoration of oil waivers and the release of all Iranian frozen assets, including those held in Qatar.
Araghchi also emphasized that reopening the strategic waterway would require recognition of a new shipping route established by Iran in coordination with Oman, as well as the closure of other routes.
He made clear that the arrangements for maritime traffic through the strait were an essential part of Iran’s proposal and that the reopening process would have to take account of the new route and the understandings reached between Iran and Oman.
The foreign minister further stressed that Tehran sought an end to the war and the cessation of hostilities across all fronts, including Lebanon. He said efforts to end the conflict should not be confined to one front while fighting continued elsewhere in the region.
Iran prepared for all possible scenarios
Turning to the prospect of renewed military confrontation, Araghchi said Iran was not ruling out the possibility of another war and was prepared for all scenarios.
“We do not rule out any possibility regarding the outbreak of war, and we are prepared for all scenarios,” he said.
He explained that Iran had used the period following the previous confrontation to strengthen its military capabilities, upgrade its equipment, address vulnerabilities and test new weapons.
Araghchi stressed that the country’s armed forces were at the highest level of readiness and that Iran was fully prepared to respond to any renewed military action.
 
He also acknowledged the impact of US economic pressure on Iran, but insisted that such pressure would not force the country to surrender or abandon its positions.
“We will continue to stand firm and resist, and we will overcome this difficult phase through our own capabilities,” he said.

CHERNIHIV, Ukraine - Evacuees from Oleshky, a bombed-out city in Russian-occupied Ukraine, told AFP that residents had to eat grass and dogs to survive and that their rescue following a humanitarian truce was a “blessing”.
US First Lady Melania Trump announced the truce on Oct 23, saying the city was “on the brink of disaster”.
Ukrainian and Russian officials visited the city together on Oct 30, delivering aid and evacuating those who wanted to leave in a rare show of cooperation between the warring sides.
Arriving in Ukraine on Oct 31 by bus, residents whom AFP interviewed painted a dire picture of life in the city.
“People were cooking grass,” said Valera, a 29-year-old former resident who did not give his last name.
“They’d grow it, as there was nothing to eat.”
He added that some residents were forced to shoot and cook dogs to survive.
“Lots of people were blown up. There were piles of bodies on the roads, loads of cars. In short, it was brutal... Terrifying,” he said.
An AFP journalist saw the residents, some draped in Ukrainian flags, disembark from buses and tearfully embrace their loved ones.
The city in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region was captured by the Russian military in 2022, and had been caught in intense fighting between the two sides that left residents starving and unable to escape.
‘They got blown up’
Yelyzaveta Paliy, who was waiting for her father to return, said she never expected him to be gone so long.
“We last saw him at the end of January 2024, when my sister, mum and I left, and he stayed behind,” the 19-year-old said.
AFP saw Paliy, her mother and sister embracing Paliy’s father in a circle.
“This is a blessing. I’ve been waiting a long time,” her father said. “There’s no life there anymore,” he said of Oleshky.
Ivan, a 70-year-old resident, said life in Oleshky had been “really bad” over the past month.
“We’ve got a vegetable garden. We grew everything we needed there. Everything ourselves, so we managed more or less. We shared with the neighbours,” he said.
“We had these specialist lads who cleared the mines themselves and set off. They drove in their cars, and they got blown up,” he said.
He said one of his relatives had lost four vehicles driving out of Oleshky.
“What else could we do? Starve to death?”
Around 2,000 residents – compared with 24,000 before Russia’s 2022 invasion – were still in Oleshky ahead of the humanitarian operation, according to Kyiv’s estimates.
Neither Moscow nor Kyiv has specified the number of people evacuated, and authorities in both countries previously indicated that many residents wished to remain in the city, even in the event of renewed fighting. AFP

Interview: South Africa eyes Chinese market as future tourism anchor: Official
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-01
01:18:22 CST
02:18:22 KST

JOHANNESBURG, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- South Africa sees strong potential for tourism growth from China and is working to improve travel access and broaden its offerings for Chinese visitors, a senior tourism official has said.
"We see it as a market that is actually going to be an anchor for us in the future," Nkhumeleni Victor Vele, director-general of South Africa's Department of Tourism, told Xinhua in an interview on Friday.
To attract more Chinese visitors, South Africa is working to improve aviation capacity and connectivity and promote its Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) system, Vele said.
South Africa officially launched the ETA in August after initially piloting it for travelers from China, India, Indonesia and Mexico during its G20 presidency last year. Eligible travelers can apply online without visiting a South African embassy or visa processing center, with applications expected to be processed within 24 hours.
Vele said China leads applications through the system, describing the uptake as an encouraging sign of renewed interest in visiting South Africa.
Beyond easier access, South Africa wants Chinese visitors to discover more of the country's distinctive experiences.
Chinese travelers are "not looking for another China outside home," Vele said. "They want an experience that is uniquely authentic, which becomes a lot more memorable over time, and therefore meaningful."
While Cape Town and Kruger National Park are already popular with Chinese tourists, the country has yet to sufficiently showcase its township and village cuisine, cultural performances and storytelling traditions, he said.
Vele highlighted the Northern Cape's desert landscapes, distinctive wildlife and plants, Karoo lamb and wines, alongside the cultural traditions of Venda communities in Limpopo's rural villages.
Such experiences should form part of South Africa's tourism packages, giving visitors a fuller understanding of the country, he said.
To help Chinese tourists enjoy these experiences comfortably, South Africa has been working to train tourist guides in Mandarin and deepen their understanding of Chinese culture, Vele said.
The efforts extend beyond language to cultural practices and sensitivities. Alongside introducing South African dishes, tourism providers also need to accommodate visitors who occasionally want familiar meals, particularly during longer stays, he said.
On further cooperation, Vele said the two sides are working on a joint marketing approach to encourage Chinese tourists to celebrate the coming Chinese New Year in South Africa.
He also called for more jointly hosted festivals and events, knowledge and information sharing, and cultural and sporting exchanges. Visitors arriving for a particular activity may then discover other attractions and experiences, he said.
Vele welcomed support from Chinese counterparts in reaching the Chinese market and called for continued cooperation, saying South Africa's door is also open to China.
"We have prepared everything for them to come and enjoy and leave with pleasant and wonderful experiences," he said. ■

ZimTrade will lead the delegation comprising businesses from horticulture, manufacturing, handicrafts, leather, construction, tourism, and e-commerce at the ninth edition of the international trade exhibition to seek new buyers, establish business partnerships, and explore opportunities from China's growing demand for imported products, the organization said in its October 2026 newsletter.

While minerals and tobacco continue to dominate Zimbabwe's exports to China, attention is increasingly shifting toward processed agricultural products, manufactured goods, and other value-added exports.
The expanded zero-tariff arrangements are expected to strengthen the competitiveness of Zimbabwean products, particularly processed foods, branded agricultural products, finished leather, and arts and crafts.
Horticulture is among the sectors showing significant potential, with macadamia nuts, citrus, avocado, and blueberries having secured market access pathways to China.

ZimTrade commended China's efforts in strengthening commercial linkages with African countries through platforms such as the CIIE, the China-Africa Economic and Trade Expo, and cross-border e-commerce channels.

NAIROBI, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- The ninth edition of the China International Import Expo (CIIE), taking place in Shanghai from Nov. 5 to 10, offers a strategic platform to advance China-Africa business ties and unlock mutual economic benefits, according to a senior banking executive.
Richard Li, deputy CEO, head of Wealth and Retail Banking (China) and group head of Global Chinese at Standard Chartered Bank, emphasized the expo's potential to inject fresh vitality into two-way Sino-African trade and investment.
"The expo is an opportunity for Kenya and other African exporters to build buyer relationships, which provides a good foundation for trade outcomes," Li said during a recent interview with Xinhua in Nairobi, the Kenyan capital.
Li noted that a key measure of the expo's success will be turning signed agreements into delivered and repeat orders, adding that Standard Chartered Bank stands ready to facilitate transactions across both markets.
African nations, including Kenya, can leverage participation at the CIIE to showcase certified, high-value and traceable agricultural products to prospective Chinese buyers, Li said.
He urged African exporters to actively track leads, finalize workable payment and delivery frameworks, and scale up capacity to fulfill incoming orders.
"That is how an initial introduction can become a lasting relationship," said Li.
"Standard Chartered can help clients align their banking arrangements with those commitments, so the timing of production, shipment and payment is considered together," he added.
From Oct. 22 to 28 this year, the bank and its partners conducted a China roadshow aimed at positioning Kenya and the broader African continent as emerging trade and investment hubs.
The roadshow also aimed to help local African enterprises expand their presence in China, strengthen their production capacity and retain greater economic value, Li said.
The bank executive noted that companies in manufacturing, agro-processing and infrastructure are pivotal to penetrating the Chinese market, emphasizing their need for reliable partners and long-term growth financing.
Li highlighted the success of the China-Kenya Trade Corridor, launched by Standard Chartered Bank in April to help local startups expand globally through tailored financing, multi-currency banking and streamlined capital management.
"The progress since then is reflected in the relationships, referrals and opportunities developed through the Kenya Investment Authority mission. These are opportunities for follow-up, rather than evidence of completed commercial transactions," Li said.
Li emphasized that the bank has served as a "super-connector," fostering dialogue between Chinese and Kenyan businesses through market expertise, tailored banking support,and the conversion of trade referrals into executed deals.
African startups and small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) will be central to the long-term sustainability of commercial ties with China, making it essential to boost export volumes and enhance local value addition, Li said.
He added that African SMEs must consistently meet Chinese quality and certification standards, secure dependable logistics, and maintain reliable production and shipping pipelines.
Li observed that reliable cold chains, stringent product certifications and dependable shipping routes will be vital to the success of African agricultural exporters targeting the Chinese market.
Over the long term, technology transfer, in-country processing and expanded local manufacturing will prove essential to enhancing their global competitiveness.
Despite ongoing geopolitical shifts, the future of Sino-African trade ties remains highly promising, Li noted, pointing to product diversification, localized value addition, resilient supply chains and proactive currency risk management as key drivers of optimism.
"The opportunity is for Africa to become a stronger engine of growth within this trading relationship, with SMEs expanding exports and building the productive capacity behind them," Li said. ■

Roundup: South Africa's Parliament condemns minibus taxi violence in Western Cape
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-11-01
01:17:58 CST
02:17:58 KST

CAPE TOWN, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- South Africa's Parliament on Saturday condemned the recent taxi violence in the Western Cape province, calling on the national bodies in the taxi industry to speedily intervene.
According to a statement issued by the Parliament, fierce violence broke out on Thursday morning in Cape Town and a number of taxi operators and drivers have reportedly been killed.
"We send our deepest condolences to the families of those who have lost their lives and wish speedy recovery to all those affected," Donald Selamolela, chairperson of the Portfolio Committee on Transport in Parliament, was quoted as saying in the statement.
"This is a sad development in our country," Selamolela said, adding that the violence came at a time when the government was doing all it could to maximize support and investment in public transport. "The last thing we need is this bout of sporadic shootings that seem to be indiscriminate," he said.
"We condemn the criminality and violence that accompanies this outbreak and we call on law enforcement to ensure and maintain visibility until calm has been restored," Selamolela said, stressing that the violence should not threaten the people's expression of their wishes in the local elections scheduled for the following week.
Five men were killed and 4 others wounded in three separate shootings across Cape Town on Thursday, including one at the Delft taxi rank, according to local media reports.
The shootings came amid a wider wave of taxi-related violence across the metro, with incidents reported in recent weeks in Gugulethu, Khayelitsha, Epping and Bonteheuwel, all located within the Cape Flats region of Cape Town.
The Cape Town International Airport experienced disruptions on Friday due to ongoing taxi-related unrest.
According to a statement issued by Airports Company South Africa (ACSA) on Friday, the unrest had affected staffing levels across airport operations, resulting in extended passenger processing times and flight delays at the airport.
ACSA said that as of 13:00 on Friday, a total of 60 flight delays had been recorded at Cape Town International Airport, comprising 44 domestic departures, 11 international departures and five arrivals. "The average delay was approximately 60 minutes, with no cancellations reported," the company said.
In a separate development, the Western Cape High Court has granted an interim interdict against two taxi associations, the Cape Amalgamated Taxi Association (CATA) and the Congress of Democratic Taxi Associations (CODETA), as well as their cited office bearers, affiliated associations and members, following recent taxi violence in the province, the Western Cape government said on Friday.
The provisional order, which takes immediate effect, prohibits "violence, intimidation, road blockades, interference with public or private transport, unlawful route takeovers, damage to property and collecting money through threats." The respondents have until Nov. 20 to show why the order should not be made final, according to the provincial government.
Western Cape Mobility Minister Isaac Sileku said the department had approached the court after other efforts to stop the violence had failed. "I have a responsibility to protect residents who rely on public transport and ensure that lawful taxi operators can work without fear," he said.
In a separate regulatory action, the Western Cape Provincial Taxi Registrar has suspended the registration of the CATA Langa Inter-township Taxi Association for six months following an inquiry into unlawful operations in the Epping area, the provincial government said.
In the Parliament's statement, Selamolela also urged taxi operators to focus on their businesses and refrain from actions that could undermine the industry, saying the shooting at the Delft taxi rank on Thursday "should never have happened."
He noted that taxis remain the only affordable mode of transport in some communities. "Our attention should be focused on making the industry affordable, safe and reliable, and importantly complementary to other forms of transport and the economy," Selamolela concluded. ■

NINGBO, China, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- DPR Korea's Ri Ryong Hyon claimed gold in the men's 75kg category at the IWF World Championships here on Saturday, while Indonesia's Abdullah Rahmat Erwin took silver after climbing from fifth place following the snatch.
Ri lifted 155kg and 160kg on his first two snatch attempts. Although he failed his third attempt at 162kg, which would have equaled the world record, he still finished atop the snatch standings. He followed with 205kg in the clean and jerk to finish first in that discipline as well, securing the overall title with a 365kg total, just one kilogram short of the world record.
After lifting 157kg, Abdullah skipped his third snatch attempt, leaving him fifth after the opening discipline. A 202kg clean and jerk brought his total to 359kg and lifted him to silver overall.
On his final attempt, Abdullah went for 207kg, a weight above the world record. In a dramatic twist, he rushed onto the platform from backstage with only five seconds remaining. He was unable to complete the lift under the time pressure.
"I already knew it's too late to lift, I don't have time to focus," said Abdullah. When asked by reporters if he would have succeeded with more time, Abdullah gave a confident reply: "I think I could."
Thailand's Wichuma Weeraphon claimed bronze with a 155kg snatch and a 200kg clean and jerk for a total of 355kg. ■

MOSCOW, Oct. 31 (Xinhua) -- Russia and Ukraine have agreed to organize regular humanitarian missions in Oleshky, a town in the Kherson region, following the completion of a joint humanitarian operation, Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova said Saturday.
The mission was the result of months of negotiations and joint efforts to help residents in need, Lantratova said in a social media post, sharing footage of humanitarian assistance being delivered to local people.
Although the mission was completed, living conditions in Oleshky remained extremely difficult, she said, calling arrangements for regular humanitarian missions "an important step forward."

"We will spare no effort to support the residents who have chosen to stay," Lantratova said.

On Oct. 23, Russia and Ukraine agreed to a temporary ceasefire in the area to facilitate aid deliveries and civilian evacuations. The ceasefire is scheduled to remain in effect until 10:59 p.m. Moscow time (1959 GMT) Sunday. ■

Major American and foreign airlines urged the US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention to reconsider new rules requiring all US-bound travellers to attest they have not been in the Democratic Republic of Congo in the prior 21 days.

Iran's Khamenei warns US and Israel against new attacks
Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the United States and Israel on Saturday against further strikes as fears mount over a resumption of fighting in the Middle East. US President Donald Trump and his Israeli ally Benjamin Netanyahu have recently threatened military action on the Islamic republic but US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump had not yet made a decision about fresh strikes.
Iran's supreme leader on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against launching new attacks following their threats to resume strikes after crucial elections, as fears mount over a return to fighting.
The declaration came as the Islamic republic's top diplomat said there were no plans to hold talks with the United States, as indirect mediation via Qatar continues.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Saturday Trump had not yet made a decision about fresh strikes.
"We can achieve military objectives if we seek to. He hasn't made a decision. I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly," Rubio said at a G20 press conference in Atlanta, Georgia.
But Rubio added that Trump "hasn't made a decision" on further military action, amid reports that the US leader could attack after key midterm elections on Tuesday.
"I have no announcement in that regard with you today, and nor do we take any of it lightly," Rubio said.
While he slammed Tehran for "actively and openly" targeting commercial vessels for attack, Rubio also expressed Trump's preference for a diplomatic solution to end war with Iran.
But he did not commit to a timeline for talks.
Watch moreReports show US and Israel are planning new strikes on Iran
US President Donald Trump had previously warned of fresh military action after the US holds midterm elections early next week, saying last weekend that he was weighing whether to "finish them off".
In Israel, which is coming off fresh elections, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has spoken of a "historic, one-time opportunity" to topple the Iranian government.
Polls in both countries could determine the direction of the conflict, with Israel having voted Tuesday but yet to form a new government.
"Any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response," Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei told top military commanders in a meeting, according to a statement.
The encounter was the first reported meeting between Khamenei and military top brass, and included armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi.
The supreme leader has not been seen publicly since before he took the helm in March after the killing of his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in US-Israeli strikes.
Khamenei also ordered commanders to update Iran's target list to include "all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy".
Iran has previously warned it would consider severing undersea cables in the Strait of Hormuz.
Petrol prices weigh on US vote
Since the initial US-Israeli strikes in February, ordinary Iranians "have been left in a state of limbo for the past year", Fariba, a Tehran housewife, told AFP.
But other residents in the Iranian capital brushed off the possible return to full-scale conflict.
"We do not fear another war. We have been at war for 48 years now," said Ebrahim, a salesman in his forties.
Since the outbreak of the war, Tehran has restricted shipping through the strategic waterway, which normally carries around one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Watch moreTrump vs MAGA: Why his movement is splitting
The blockade has caused a spike in global energy prices, making the war unpopular among the US public ahead of midterm congressional elections Tuesday.
Gains for the opposition Democrats could restrict, to an extent, Trump's ability to enact policy.
Voting in Israel has left Netanyahu's political camp with the most seats in parliament but short of a majority, leaving the make-up of the next administration unclear.
Read more'Atmosphere of fear': Trump moves to curtail voting rights ahead of the midterms
'Flames of war'
The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran. The Islamic republic swiftly responded with attacks on American assets in countries around the region.
Fresh diplomatic efforts are underway to avert any resumption of fighting, with Qatari mediators landing in Tehran on Friday, and US Vice President JD Vance sending a letter to Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei.
But Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Saturday that "currently, there are no plans for meetings with American officials".
"Iran's conditions are clear, and consultations regarding them are ongoing among mediators," he said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA.

Qatar and Pakistan have been mediating between the warring parties, but the talks have yet to produce a lasting agreement.
The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance had sent his letter to Iran's security chief at Trump's direction in a bid to revive negotiations and avert further US strikes.
Araghchi confirmed that Iran received the letter, saying, "The American side's effort to open a dialogue and reach a broader understanding is viewed as a positive step."
But the Iranian side kept firm its warnings against further attacks.
Earlier on Saturday, army spokesman Mohammad Akaraminia said that any resumption of hostilities would only expand the scope of the war.
"The flames of war will undoubtedly engulf a much wider geographical area," he said on social media, without elaborating.
Araghchi warned on X of an "Earth-shattering blow Iran's Powerful Armed Forces will deal against those who dare harm our people".
He said there would no longer be any "red lines".

China expands foreign business access at world's largest FTP
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-31
16:58:51 UTC
01:58:51 KST

Under the measures, foreign physicians legally licensed to practice medicine overseas may obtain permits to provide clinical diagnosis and treatment services in Hainan for up to three years, with extensions available in accordance with relevant regulations.
More convenient policies regarding work permits and stay and residence will also be introduced for foreign nationals.
The Hainan FTP, located in China's southernmost island province, launched island-wide special customs operations in December 2025, allowing freer entry of overseas goods, expanded zero-tariff coverage and more business-friendly measures as part of China's efforts to promote high-standard opening-up.
Overseas companies will be allowed to use bonded facilities at Hainan's liquefied natural gas (LNG) receiving terminals, while the FTP will be supported in conducting LNG futures delivery warehouse operations after LNG futures contracts are launched.
Other measures include promoting offshore trade, expanding the range of products eligible for bonded maintenance, facilitating the entry of eligible bonded remanufactured products into pilot free trade zones on the Chinese mainland, encouraging the use of the yuan in new forms of barter trade, and deepening the FTP's economic and trade cooperation with China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Bonded remanufactured products entering mainland pilot free trade zones will be subject to applicable import tariffs, import-related value-added tax and consumption tax. They must also meet all applicable technical requirements for equivalent new products and relevant regulations on remanufactured products, and be clearly labeled as such.
The circular also calls for improved insurance products and services in areas such as international transportation and bonded maintenance.
The latest measures come amid robust growth in Hainan's foreign trade. In the first three quarters of 2026, the province's goods imports and exports reached 285.44 billion yuan (about 42.5 billion U.S. dollars), up 49.8 percent year on year, while trade in services rose 11.7 percent to 56.95 billion yuan, according to data from Hainan's provincial commerce authorities.
Trade in maintenance and repair services more than doubled year on year to 3.31 billion yuan during the same period, according to the provincial commerce department. The trade mainly came from imports of aircraft materials and components and revenues from aircraft maintenance services.
The number of newly established foreign-invested enterprises in Hainan rose 38.6 percent year on year in the first half of 2026, according to the State Administration for Market Regulation.
The FTP measures are part of China's broader efforts to promote high-standard opening-up. The country has announced plans to further expand pilot opening-up programs in sectors such as value-added telecommunications, biotechnology and wholly foreign-owned hospitals, while taking steps to facilitate cross-border trade and investment.
The circular was jointly issued by the Ministry of Commerce, the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment and the General Administration of Customs.

But we guarantee you that this is a temporary phenomenon," he said.The Congress leader insisted that Gyanesh Kumar was only one among several people the opposition held responsible for what it described as an assault on the country's democratic institutions."We are not going to let you escape. I also want to address the people who have carried out this assault on the Union of India. Gyanesh Kumar is just one element; there are many others. We know who they are, and we understand deeply who they are," Rahul Gandhi said."This is a warning to you: things are shifting. Please hear this warning and realise that this is a new political weapon sitting in the garden, and this weapon is going to hurt you very badly if you continue down your path," he said."I am saying this with love and affection; we are not nasty or evil people, but we will protect the Constitution and the voice of our people."Rahul Gandhi also backed the demand for legal action against the CEC, saying Gyanesh Kumar should not only face impeachment but also be tried in court for treason."I fully support the motion that Mr Gyanesh Kumar should not only be impeached but should also be tried in a court of law for treason so that justice can be served," he said.
INDIA bloc holds 'public impeachment' of CEC
Rahul Gandhi's remarks came at an unprecedented INDIA bloc event in which opposition MPs and leaders, along with civil society representatives, passed a resolution seeking Gyanesh Kumar's impeachment and accusing him of facilitating the deletion of voters' names to influence election outcomes.The symbolic proceedings were held at the lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence at 10, Rajaji Marg in New Delhi. Former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar presided over the meeting, which was organised in a setting resembling parliamentary proceedings.The resolution was moved by Kharge, seconded by Samajwadi Party leader Harendra Malik and supported by Rahul Gandhi and several other opposition MPs and civil society members. It was adopted unanimously by a show of hands.Around 250 opposition MPs, civil society representatives and mediapersons attended the event. Some people who alleged that their names had been wrongly deleted from electoral rolls were also present.Rahul Gandhi acknowledged that holding what resembled parliamentary proceedings outside Parliament might appear unusual, but said the opposition had been left with little choice."I don't think anything like this has ever happened in history," he said, adding that the gathering of opposition leaders and civil society members in a garden might appear absurd."But we had no other option, as every single institution is closed to us," he said.The stage was designed to resemble the old Lok Sabha chamber, with a wooden-panelled backdrop and seats arranged in a semi-circular formation.Kharge, who moved the motion, alleged that the right to vote was under threat because the Election Commission was functioning at the behest of PM Modi and Shah. He accused the poll panel of failing to act independently and raised concerns over alleged electoral manipulation.
BJP calls it 'mockery' of democracy
The BJP hit back at the opposition's symbolic proceedings, accusing the INDIA bloc of making a mockery of Parliament and democratic institutions.
BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra took a swipe at Rahul Gandhi, alleging that the Congress was repeatedly attempting to launch its leader politically without success."Go ahead and hold your mock Parliament or take out your marches; the world has already understood that Rahul Gandhi simply lacks the fuel. This 'satellite' is never going to launch," Patra said.He added that the opposition could have Gandhi as a "mock Prime Minister for life".

French police clash with some protesters again as demonstrations continue in nation's cities
French police fired tear gas and clashed with some protesters on Saturday as thousands marched across France again in largely peaceful demonstrations against soaring living costs and police violence.
Police said about 70,000 people demonstrated in Paris alone. France's interior ministry said about 320,000 people rallied nationwide.
In the southern port city of Marseille, demonstrators clashed with police. In Lyon, France's third-largest city, people threw projectiles at police, prompting officers to fire tear gas, according to a journalist at the scene. In the southern city of Toulouse, police used water cannon against an unauthorized protest that drew several thousand people, mostly young demonstrators, some of them in costume.
Authorities in France reported more than 560 arrests nationwide by Saturday night, The Associated Press reported. Police had arrested thousands of people following riots and looting that marred marches the previous two Saturdays.
In Paris, thousands of people, some wearing costumes ranging from Spider-Man to Frankenstein, walked through eastern Paris as a helicopter circled overhead. Placards read: "No need for tear gas to make our future look bleak" and "Dressed up as an angry citizen for Halloween." Hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, who has accused French President Emmanuel Macron's government of "taking an increasingly authoritarian turn," joined the march.
"We say no to the cost of living, no to the far right, yes to high school students' demands, yes to giving citizens a voice," Camille Guerin, 31, said in the western city of Nantes.
In the northern French city of Lille, 47-year-old Aurelie Herrmann danced at the protest.
"I dance because on television they only show damage and destruction, whereas you can perfectly well demonstrate in good spirits," she said.
An aide to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday that police had prepared for street violence on a scale "comparable" to the unrest two weeks ago, when shops were looted and public buildings set ablaze. Nunez said authorities had detected social media calls for Halloween gatherings on Saturday evening that urged protesters to spark a "revolution."
Some shopkeepers again prepared by barricading their businesses.
"Everyone is staying home. No one is going to come and buy anything," said Wael Boubaker, a cafe employee in eastern Paris, as he covered a storefront with plywood panels.
Alain Di Crescenzo, president of France's chamber of commerce, said business owners were worried.
"Shopkeepers can't wait for Saturday to be over," Di Crescenzo told broadcaster France Inter.
Protests come as elections near
The demonstrations come in a febrile political climate, with presidential elections less than six months away and far-right leader Marine Le Pen leading the polls.
The protest movement, bringing together activists, trade unions, and high school and university students, initially focused on the rising cost of living, inequality, and deteriorating learning conditions.
Following a security clampdown and serious injuries to some protesters, the movement broadened its demands to include greater protection of civil liberties and the right to protest. This week, student protesters complained that the police did not authorize a march through the center of the French capital, and vowed to stage new blockades of high schools and universities next week.
With the eurozone's second-largest economy on the brink of recession and under pressure to rein in its debt, the government has limited scope to appease protesters through additional spending.
Similar youth-led demonstrations have been seen across Europe in recent weeks. Thousands of young Germans took to the streets nationwide on Saturday.

Iranian strikes damage 24 US military sites, adding billions to war costs: WSJ
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-31
16:50:07 UTC
01:50:07 KST

Iranian strikes have damaged hundreds of buildings at military installations hosting US forces across the Middle East, potentially adding billions of dollars to the cost of the war, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
An analysis of satellite imagery found that 274 structures at 24 installations with a US military presence sustained damage during the war's first six months.
Among the hardest-hit sites was Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan, where an Iranian strike on July 17 killed three American service members and damaged at least 19 buildings, including facilities where troops sleep.
The Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated that rebuilding the damaged structures alone would cost more than $4 billion, excluding the replacement of equipment and systems inside the buildings.
Meanwhile, the Pentagon has put the damage to US military bases at a minimum of $5 billion, with estimates potentially reaching $15 billion, according to US officials cited by the Journal.
These expenses come on top of the estimated $47.1 billion cost of the war as of October 16, the report said.
Beyond the financial burden, the destruction has raised concerns over the safety of military personnel, with more than 20 US servicemembers killed and over 400 wounded since the conflict began February 28.
Opposition Democrats in the US have accused the Trump administration of deliberately low-balling figures on the cost of the war, from casualties to its budgetary and wider financial costs.

MAC details stark Taiwan-China divide
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-31
16:44:06 UTC
01:44:06 KST

The fifth plenum of the Chinese Communist Party’s (CCP) 20th Central Committee and Taiwan’s election debates highlighted a stark contrast between China’s centralization of power and Taiwan’s democracy, Mainland Affairs Council (MAC) Deputy Minister Shen Yu-chung (沈有忠) said yesterday.
Differences in political systems are the most fundamental issue in cross-strait relations, which have nothing to do with similarities in culture, language or ethnicity, he said.
Shen made the remarks at a forum held by the Secure Taiwan Associate Corporation to discuss possible developments in China’s domestic political situation following the fifth plenum, and their implications for Taiwan.
Photo: Fang Wei-li, Taipei Times
The theme of the plenum, which concluded on Thursday last week, was “unswerving promotion of the full and rigorous party self-governance,” a move by Chinese President Xi Jinping (習近平) to further bolster the CCP’s leadership and consolidate his authority ahead of next year’s 21st CCP National Congress, Shen said.
The MAC’s analysis of the plenum can be summarized into four points, he said.
First, the “Xi Jinping thought on party building” was established as a political guiding principle, further consolidating Xi’s unchallengeable position as the party’s leader, Shen said.
The plenum confirmed earlier decisions to expel 33 officials from the party, including former senior military leaders Zhang Youxia (張又俠) and Liu Zhenli (劉振立), he said, adding that accusations against them, including failing to implement central policies and engaging in duplicity and disloyalty, demonstrated that anyone who is insufficiently loyal to Xi or deviates from his ideology and directives would be purged.
Second, the MAC believes that “strict party governance” aims to ensure the CCP’s long-term rule and preserve its one-party dictatorship, Shen said.
Whether it is political, organizational, integrity or work discipline, all rules must be based on monitoring and ensuring that party members and officials obey the CCP, he said, adding that the development of China’s constitutional system, and the protection of people’s rights and interests take a back seat to the goal of consolidating the CCP’s one-party rule.
Third, the promotion of “the party’s self-revolution” represents a rejection of external oversight by the public, media and civil society, Shen said.
Although the authenticity of posts that students from more than 10 Chinese universities had allegedly signed a petition calling for the abolition of the indefinite term for the president remains unverified, they signaled that the party’s leadership is not subject to any external oversight, he said.
Xi might respond to academic activities or social movements with further legal measures or intensified surveillance, he added.
The CCP has fully internalized its oversight mechanisms within the party’s disciplinary and supervisory systems, rejecting democratic checks and balances in the name of “self-correction within the party,” he said.
Fourth, moves to eliminate dissenting voices have paved the way for Xi to secure a fourth term at next year’s 21st National Congress, Shen said.
The number of Central Committee members and alternate members absent from the plenum reached a new high since the era of Mao Zedong (毛澤東), he said.
Large-scale purges of senior party, government and military officials over the past few years have removed potential political obstacles to Xi’s ambitions, ensuring he can continue on to a fourth term with the party’s full endorsement, he added.
While the plenum unfolded in Beijing, many in Taiwan were focused on the mayoral debates in Taipei and Kaohsiung, highlighting the fundamental differences between the political systems on the two sides of the Strait, Shen said.
The CCP’s fifth plenum demonstrated the consolidation of power and the growing dominance of Xi’s leadership, he said, adding that Taiwan’s lively mayoral debates would be impossible in China.
Shen urged Taiwanese to recognize these institutional differences and unite against authoritarian aggression, build a shared commitment to protecting freedom, democracy and national sovereignty to ensure that Taiwan can continue to deepen its democracy, prosperity and development amid the CCP’s multifaceted pressure campaign.
With local elections entering their final campaign phase, the government would continue to closely monitor developments within the CCP and shifts in its power structure, while preventing and exposing various forms of Chinese election interference, he said.
It will also continue to counter China’s cognitive warfare, transnational repression and attempts to infiltrate and divide Taiwanese society, while defending national sovereignty, freedom, security and the democratic way of life, he added.

Warm and dry weather is expected today before two more waves of seasonal winds bring rain to windward areas and overnight lows in northern Taiwan to about 20°C this week, the Central Weather Administration (CWA) said yesterday.
Seasonal winds were expected to weaken last night, bringing drier conditions and isolated showers to eastern Taiwan, CWA forecaster Wang Pin-hsiang (王品翔) said.
Wang said that seasonal winds are expected to strengthen again tomorrow and on Tuesday, then weaken on Wednesday and Thursday before another wave arrives on Friday or Saturday. Rain is likely along the northern coast and in eastern Taiwan during this time.
Photo provided by the Central Weather Administration
Although Typhoon In-fa is not forecast to directly affect Taiwan, it could create significant swells along the northern coast, eastern Taiwan and the Hengchun Peninsula (恆春半島) from today into next week, Wang added.

However, its effects are expected to bring long waves to the northern coast of Keelung, coastal areas in eastern Taiwan, including Orchid Island (Lanyu, 蘭嶼) and Green Island (綠島), and the Hengchun Peninsula starting tomorrow, he said.

Many people love their dogs and spare no effort to provide them with the best food possible. However, a recent study has shed light on an often overlooked environmental issue. By analyzing nearly 1,000 commercial dog food recipes, researchers found that these diets leave a significant “carbon pawprint.” For a 20-kilogram dog, 40% of tested dog foods were found to produce more greenhouse gas emissions than __1__ from a human vegan diet.
The primary factor is the composition and format of modern dog food, particularly wet and raw diets. Products made with meat that is also commonly __2__ humans, such as chicken breast, require more resources and create more greenhouse gases. By contrast, foods containing animal byproducts or plant proteins generally have a smaller environmental impact. Compared with standard dry kibble, wet and raw products also __3__ on the environment. They often require refrigeration or freezing and involve additional packaging and transportation.
__4__ popular belief, raw diets are not always the healthiest option. They may pose health risks, including nutritional imbalances and bacterial infections. When properly formulated, plant-based diets can also meet dogs’ nutritional needs. Although these options are not yet widely used, they are gaining acceptance among veterinarians.
Photo: AdobeStock I 照片：AdobeStock
This research indicates that the environmental impact of dog food depends largely on its ingredients. Therefore, clear labels must be placed on packaging. Consumers need __5__ ingredient information to make informed choices, and such clarity would also help buyers balance nutrition with sustainability.
許多人深愛自己的狗狗，不遺餘力地盡可能為牠們提供最好的食物。然而，近期的一項研究揭示了一個往往被忽視的環境議題。透過分析近一千種市售狗糧配方，研究人員發現這些飲食留下了顯著的「碳爪跡」。以一隻二十公斤的狗而言，在接受測試的狗糧中，發現有 40% 所產生的溫室氣體排放量甚至超過了人類純素飲食的排放量。
主要的因素在於現代狗糧的成分與形式，尤其是溼食和生食。使用人類也常食用的肉類（例如雞胸肉）所製成的產品，需要消耗更多資源，也會產生更多溫室氣體。相比之下，含有動物副產品或植物蛋白的食物，通常對環境的影響較小。與普通的乾飼料相比，溼食與生食產品對環境造成的負擔也更重。這些產品往往需要冷藏或冷凍，還包含額外的包裝與運輸。
與普遍的觀念相反，生食飲食並不總是最健康的選擇。它們可能會帶來健康風險，包括營養失衡和細菌感染。在經過妥善調配的情況下，植物性飲食同樣能夠滿足狗狗的營養需求。雖然這些選項目前尚未被廣泛使用，但已逐漸獲得獸醫們的認可。
這項研究指出，狗糧對環境的影響在很大程度上取決於其成分。因此，包裝上必須貼有清楚的標籤。消費者需要公開透明的成分資訊來做出明智的選擇，而這樣的清晰度也將有助於購買者在營養與永續發展之間取得平衡。
What Did You Learn?
1. (A) which (B) these (C) what (D) those
2. (A) restricted to (B) consumed by (C) satisfied with (D) prohibited from
3. (A) make a smaller profit (B) cast a lesser shadow (C) place a heavier burden (D) score a better success
4. (A) Contrary to (B) Prior to (C) Because of (D) Short of
5. (A) eloquent (B) imaginative (C) transparent (D) predictable
答案： 1. D 2. B 3. C 4. A 5. C
Words in Use
1. carbon n. 碳
carbon pawprint （碳爪跡）是從carbon footprint（碳足跡）衍生出的環保新詞。
carbon footprint 通常是指人類活動或產品生命週期中所排放的溫室氣體總量。
carbon pawprint 則指我們飼養的寵物在生活中所產生的碳排放量，除了文中提到的寵物食品，還包括日常用品、醫療和廢棄物等。
The bike frame is made of carbon fiber, which makes it very light and strong.
這輛自行車的車架是由碳纖維製成，讓它非常輕巧又堅固。
2. overlook vt. 忽略，忽視（本文為過去分詞作形容詞用）
This small town is an often overlooked tourist destination with beautiful scenery.
這座小鎮是個景色優美卻經常被忽略的旅遊景點。
Julian overlooked the spelling mistake on the first page of the essay.
朱利安忽略了作文第一頁的拼字錯誤。
3. analyze vt. 分析
Doctors will analyze your blood sample to find out what is causing your allergy.
醫生會分析你的血液樣本，以找出導致你過敏的原因。
4. emission n. 排放物
The new hybrid bus reduces smoke emissions.
這款新型油電混合公車降低了廢氣排放物。
5. composition n. 組合成分
Scientists are studying the chemical composition of the soil on Mars.
科學家們正在研究火星土壤的化學成分。
Practical Phrases
1. spare no effort to V 不遺餘力地……
Becca spares no effort to achieve her dream of studying abroad.
貝卡不遺餘力地去實現出國留學的夢想。
2. shed light on. . . 闡明;使人明白
The discovery of the old sign sheds light on the local history of the farm.
這塊舊招牌的發現讓人們更了解這塊農田的當地歷史。
3. by contrast 相較之下（相反）
Kevin is very quiet and shy; by contrast, his sister Sarah loves to talk.
凱文非常安靜害羞；相較之下，他妹妹莎拉非常健談。
4. compared with / to. . . 與……相比
Compared with the old system, the new software is very easy to use.
與舊系統相比，新軟體非常容易使用。
5. balance A with B 在A與B間取得平衡
Rachel learned to balance her studies with her social life.
瑞秋學會在課業與社交生活間取得平衡。

Experts caution cancer cachexia an urgent issue
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-31
16:44:00 UTC
01:44:00 KST

Many people might think it is normal to experience weight loss and weakness during cancer treatment, but medical experts yesterday warned that it could also be “cancer cachexia,” and that insufficient muscle mass can even cause treatment to fail.
The 3rd International Conference on Sarcopenia, organized by Taipei Medical University (TMU) and focusing on “Sarcopenia, Cachexia and Frailty” was held at the university in Taipei yesterday.
With the global population aging, sarcopenia has become a pressing health challenge that significantly impacts the well-being and quality of life of elderly people, and surveys in Taiwan estimate that more than one-third of elderly people are affected or at risk, the TMU said.
Photo courtesy fo the Taipei Medical University
Experts from the UK, Japan, South Korea and Singapore, across sectors and disciplines — covering neurology, rehabilitation, cardiology, regenerative medicine, biomarkers, genetics and more — joined the conference to address this urgent issue, it said.
Some people become increasingly thin and frail during cancer treatment and believe that it is a normal side effect, but TMU Graduate Institute of Cancer Biology and Drug Discovery chair professor Yen Yun (閻雲) said it could be a sign of “cancer cachexia.”
Cancer cachexia is a tumor-driven metabolic syndrome that is characterized by systemic inflammation, which accelerates the breakdown of muscle mass and fat tissue, he said.
People with cancer cachexia might experience extreme weight loss and exhaustion, and it could even force the patients to discontinue cancer treatments because their body is no longer strong enough to tolerate them, he added.
Studies have estimated that cancer cachexia affects about 50 percent of people with cancer, Yen said.
In his keynote speech, National Cancer Centre of Singapore deputy chief executive officer Bin Tean Teh said that muscle loss occurred in cancer patients through transcriptomics, and shared exploratory pathways for future treatments.
TMU executive vice president Liou Tsan-hon (劉燦宏), who is also TMU Shuang Ho Hospital superintendent, said preserving muscle mass has become a public issue, as in a super-aged society, “maintaining muscle strength and preventing disability” is the key to health and longevity.
As people age, inactivity causes muscle mass and strength to decline much faster, and continued muscle loss might ultimately severely impair their ability to manage daily self-care, he said.
As there is no medication that can directly cure or treat sarcopenia globally, early lifestyle interventions combining a “nutritional diet” and “resistance exercise” have become a shared focus of preventing and managing age-related muscle loss, he said.

2026 Elections: Kaohsiung debate focuses on 205th Arsenal, donations
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-31
16:43:59 UTC
01:43:59 KST

A mayoral debate was on Friday evening held in Kaohsiung, with the two leading candidates — the Democratic Progressive Party’s (DPP) Lai Jui-lung (賴瑞隆) and Chinese Nationalist Party’s (KMT) Ko Chih-en (柯志恩) — focusing largely on the redevelopment of the site of the 205th Arsenal and political donations.
The relocation of the 205th Arsenal, under the Armaments Bureau, from downtown Kaohsiung to the city’s Dashu District (大樹) was completed last year. Plans for the redevelopment of the 57-hectare site have since drawn considerable public attention.
Founded in 1945, the 205th Arsenal has been responsible for producing small arms with calibers of less than 40mm for the armed forces.
Photo: CNA
The arsenal is near Asia New Bay Area, which the city has developed into a major commercial and industrial hub, Lai said, adding that the site should therefore be reserved for future industrial development.
He criticized Ko’s proposal to relocate Kaohsiung City Hall and the Kaohsiung City Council to the former arsenal site, saying that the plan would impose a heavy financial burden on the city.
Ko said Lai had no clear idea how to redevelop the vast site.
He only offered incomplete proposals without careful consideration, such as seeking to attract Nvidia Corp to the area or turning it into an artificial intelligence park, she said.
The former arsenal is in the heart of the city and a comprehensive redevelopment plan is needed, Ko said.
She suggested transforming the site into a special district similar to New York City’s Manhattan, with the ambition of making it surpass Taipei’s Xinyi (信義) commercial district.
Ko, a legislator, questioned Lai, also a legislator, over donations he had received from solar energy developers and his arrangement of legislative hearings that allegedly benefited their business interests.
Lai said he had always declared political donations according to law.
The hearings were organized to seek expert opinions from government officials, academics and business representatives on the direction of Taiwan’s energy development, rather than to promote the interests of particular companies, he said.
Lai also criticized the KMT for introducing a proposal to increase the government’s revenue allocation to Taipei by 3 percent when the legislature amended the Act Governing the Allocation of Government Revenues and Expenditures (財政收支劃分法) in 2024.
Ko said the amendment passed by the legislature contained no provision for a 3 percent increase in Taipei’s revenue allocation, accusing Lai of spreading rumors and making personal attacks against her.
Lai said Ko did not know Kaohsiung well enough, urging voters to vote for him, so he could work for the city, arguing that Kaohsiung could not afford development policies that favored northern Taiwan over the south.
He accused Ko of claiming to put Kaohsiung first while prioritizing the KMT’s interests.
Ko responded that, as a legislator-at-large, her work in politics and policy proposals covered national issues, including energy, education and school council reform.

Countries commit to get nature goals back on track
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-31
16:43:48 UTC
01:43:48 KST

Nearly 200 nations on Friday struck hard-fought agreements at a UN biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity’s destructive toll on nature.
Delegates cheered as crucial texts were approved in overtime, but the celebrations were tempered by acrimonious debates and regret over limited progress on some of the most contentious issues.
The COP17 summit in Armenia sought to revive a landmark commitment to halt and reverse the destruction of nature by 2030 after global efforts to meet that goal fell short.
Photo: AFP
Over two bruising weeks in Yerevan, nations were urged to correct course to keep the pact alive and protect the plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth.
The UN had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30 percent of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation.
“And that’s it. Perfect,” COP17 president and Armenian Minister of Environment Hambardzum Matevosyan said as he brought down the gavel on two major texts, the final versions of which were still not available early yesterday.
However, the outcome was “not commensurate” with the crisis engulfing the natural world, French Minister of Ecological Transition Monique Barbut said.
“The progress we failed to achieve here is a series of missed opportunities to speed up our response to the loss of biodiversity,” Barbut said, adding that “nature will not wait for the pace of our negotiations.”
The final plenary stretched through Friday night and well into yesterday morning, with negotiations turning sour as the hours dragged on. Even as some delegates left to catch flights, others stayed behind to argue technical points.
UN Convention on Biological Diversity Executive Secretary Astrid Schomaker said the summit had achieved some “quite remarkable things at a moment when multilateralism is supposedly not functioning.”
“Some of these more difficult subjects, we could not expect to have strong negotiated commitments. That was never the plan,” she said.
A draft agreement said nations were urged to “accelerate” their efforts and warned that “increased action” was needed to tackle the forces driving biodiversity loss.
This “represents a positive outcome... and though there are weaknesses, particularly on harmful subsidies, it does represent a step forward,” Guido Broekhoven from WWF International said.
Tackling subsidies and other incentives that encourage activities harmful to nature — such as fossil fuels, intensive agriculture and overfishing — was one of the most politically fraught agenda items at the summit.
A rare fight over science cast a pall over the summit, with a number of countries accused of undermining efforts to approve key reports in scenes that shocked even seasoned negotiators.
“We regret the increasing instances in which scientific evidence and its uptake has been challenged or constrained” by politics, Swiss negotiator Gabriela Blatter said. “Our delegations fully respect every state’s right to safeguard national interest, but science is not negotiable.”
A separate row revolved around finding new cash sources to fund conservation efforts — another hot-button issue with public budgets under strain amid an energy crisis and conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.
The EU led a charge for wealthy emerging economies such as China to contribute to global conservation efforts, a contentious issue at COP17.
In a sign of a possible compromise, another draft text invited countries outside the developed-country donors to voluntarily join the group.
Outstanding questions over the design of the Cali Fund — a UN mechanism that hoped to attract billions of dollars in corporate contributions, but is close to empty — were left unresolved.
The COP17 summit has decided that Ecuador would host the next biodiversity talks in 2028 after the South American nation defeated Panama in a secret vote.
